Nov 3 : World number one Elena Rybakina and American Coco Gauff were drawn in Group One for the WTA Finals, while second-ranked Aryna Sabalenka will face third-ranked Mirra Andreeva in Group Two at the season-ending championship.  Defending champion Rybakina will begin her title defense against Gauff, four-time WTA Finals participant Jessica Pegula and reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, who is making her tournament debut. Sabalenka's group also includes 19-year-old Andreeva, 2018 WTA Finals champion Elina Svitolina and Czech Karolina Muchova. The event, which brings together the season's top eight qualifiers, will be held at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden from November 8 to 15. The top two players from each round-robin group will advance to the semifinals.

Rybakina, who claimed the world number one ranking after September's US Open, said the position brought both added scrutiny and motivation. "It has been an unbelievable couple of months," Rybakina said during Tuesday's draw ceremony. "It is of course pressure because of all of the attention, but at the same time it's motivation because you don't want to lose. In this sport, you still need to work a lot." Sabalenka will be looking for vengeance after losing her top ranking to Rybakina at the US Open. The Belarusian won both Indian Wells and Miami earlier this year to complete the "Sunshine Double." In July, organizers announced the tournament would move from Riyadh to Indian Wells following the early end of the WTA's hosting agreement with Saudi Arabia.

COPENHAGEN: Greenland's parliament on Tuesday (Nov 3) ratified the Arctic island's security agreement struck earlier this year with US President Donald Trump, although some opposition party members questioned the deal's economic value. The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September, aimed at ending tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory. The deal expands the US military's role in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. A majority of lawmakers had already signalled support for the deal in a first debate last month.

Tuesday's vote was 16 in favour and none against, with seven abstentions. The White House in January said Trump was discussing options for acquiring Greenland, including potential use of the US military, alarming governments in Europe and triggering intense diplomatic efforts to calm the situation. Greenlandic Foreign Minister Mute Egede said on Tuesday that ratification of the deal was an important step for the island. "We must accept that peace and stability are no longer something we can take for granted," Egede told lawmakers in Nuuk shortly before the vote. Opposition party Naleraq, the most prominent political voice for Greenland's independence, questioned the deal's economic value during the debate. "We are looking for a better agreement that we can benefit from when we become an independent state. But no economic benefit has been gained from the agreement," Naleraq chair Pele Broberg said. The Danish parliament is due to give the bill a first reading on Nov 11, followed by a second reading and a vote on Nov 19. The executive agreement will enter into force once Denmark and Greenland have ratified it, and does not require approval from the US Senate.

TOKYO, Nov 4 : Japan Investment Corp (JIC), a state-backed fund, plans to sell chipmaking materials maker JSR to Mitsui Chemicals in a deal that could exceed 1.3 trillion yen ($8.20 billion), two people familiar with the matter said. A decision could come as soon as within the month, one of the people said. Both people declined to be identified as the information is not public. JIC, JSR and Mitsui Chemicals did not reply to a request for comment. Shares in Mitsui Chemicals fell 7 per cent following Reuters' report. Reuters, which previously reported JIC is considering selling JSR, is reporting the final buyer for the first time.

JIC acquired JSR for some 900 billion yen two years ago and had said it planned to use the business to drive consolidation in the semiconductor materials sector. The fund will instead sell JSR to a domestic chemical major as it takes advantage of a lift in the valuation of chip-related firms due to a boom in AI investment. JSR, established in 1957, is a leading manufacturer of photoresists which are used to transfer circuit patterns onto semiconductor wafers. Mitsui Chemicals, which is also expanding its chip materials business, has a market capitalisation of about 800 billion yen. The deal could be among the largest in Japan's chemicals sector, exceeding the 2020 acquisition of Hitachi Chemical by Showa Denko which created Resonac Holdings. Mitsui Chemicals had 217.8 billion yen in cash and cash equivalents and 876.4 billion yen in interest-bearing debt as at the end of June. Its debt-to-equity ratio, a measure of financial soundness, stood at 0.75. JIC, which is overseen by the trade ministry, was set up in 2018 to invest in companies with the goal of boosting Japan's competitiveness. Its investments include medical equipment maker Topcon alongside private equity firm KKR. ($1 = 158.5200 yen)

Nov 3 : Puerto Rico's Amanda Serrano said on Tuesday she wants to be remembered as a game changer ahead of her farewell fight against Australia's Skye Falzon on home soil next year.  The seven-division world champion will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight world titles against Falzon at Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan on January 9, in a bout that Most Valuable Promotions has dubbed "The Last Walk".  Serrano, who owns a 50-4-1 record with 32 knockouts, previously announced she will retire after the fight.  "I want people to remember me as a game changer," Serrano said at a press conference in San Juan. "I gave it my all in the ring. Every time I fought, every time I trained, I just left everything in the ring, and I hope that you guys see that when I do fight."

Serrano has been a champion of equality in boxing over the years. She is the first and only Puerto Rican boxer, male or female, to become undisputed world champion, and in 2022 made history with Ireland's Katie Taylor when they became the first women boxers to headline New York's Madison Square Garden. The 38-year-old also defeated Brazil's Danila Ramos in 2023 in the first-ever women’s unified world championship contested over 12 three-minute rounds, which is equal to a men’s championship fight.  HISTORIC HOMECOMING More history is on the line for Serrano as she chases the women's knockout record, which she jointly shares with American Christy Martin. While Serrano said it would be the "cherry on top", she also insisted she wants to make the most of her final appearance in the ring, at a venue she has always dreamed of fighting in.  "I made sure that I went back to the 12 three-minute rounds because I want to enjoy every second, every minute of my last fight in there," Serrano said. "I'm going to go out there and give it my all. If the knockout comes, it comes." Falzon, who holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts, said it was a dream come true to get the tap to fight Serrano.  "I actually cried about it," Falzon said. "The opportunity is something I'm going to grab hold of and I just can't wait." For the 38-year-old Australian, that means betting on herself rather than simply participating in the final chapter of Serrano's storied career.  "I'm not here just to take part in Amanda's history, I'm here to try to write my own," Falzon said. "I wouldn't be a fighter if I didn't believe I could win."  Serrano welcomed the confidence from the Australian.  "I wouldn't like if any of my opponents would come thinking they're going to come to lose," she said. "I love to fight the best out there." Serrano, who was born in Carolina, said her decision to retire simply boiled down to time and that she always knew she would hang up her gloves in Puerto Rico.  "You guys (have) been with me from the very beginning, supporting me, loving me, and I've been fighting for you guys," she said.  "I bring my flag with me, it's in my heart. I'm always with you, and I fight for you. I just want you guys to celebrate my long journey, and it's going to be a great night."

Source: Reuters

Nov 3 : Block on Tuesday raised its full-year gross profit outlook after strength in its Cash App unit lifted the firm's quarterly earnings, while also reaching a preliminary settlement with the US Department of Justice over its anti-money laundering program. Shares of the Jack Dorsey-led company rose 7 per cent in extended trading. The US economy grew at its fastest pace in a year in the third quarter, shrugging off higher oil prices due to the Iran war, signaling that consumers maintained robust spending, benefiting financial firms such as Block. Gross profit at Cash App, Block's consumer-focused financial platform, surged 27 per cent in the third quarter from a year earlier. Gross profit at its Square merchant business rose 14 per cent.

Cash App's growing banking and lending products have helped Block diversify its revenue streams beyond transaction fees. "We've seen continued strong spending on Cash App Card as well as strong repayment rates on Borrow, which for us are the signals that collectively tell us consumers are managing their finances and the strength of their pocketbook," Chief Financial Officer Amrita Ahuja told Reuters in an interview. But the diversification has also increased the company's credit losses. Block's losses on transaction, loan and consumer receivables rose 65.6 per cent to $601.7 million in the third quarter. Block now expects gross profit of $12.63 billion for 2026, representing 22 per cent growth, compared with its prior forecast of $12.51 billion. It forecast gross profit of $3.32 billion for the fourth quarter. The fintech firm also forecast 2027 gross profit of $14.52 billion, implying 15 per cent growth, as it expects AI investments to drive sustained growth. Executive Officer and Head of Business Owen Jennings said the company expects the fourth quarter to mark the first time it generates revenue directly from AI tools. Adjusted operating income rose to $923 million, or $1.13 per share, for the three months ended September 30, compared with $480 million, or 54 cents per share, a year earlier. REGULATORY OVERHANG EASES Separately, Block said it reached an agreement in principle with the US Department of Justice in October to defer for three years a charge that the company failed to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program in violation of the Bank Secrecy Act. The deferred prosecution agreement could result in an expected net payment of roughly $764 million after credits for prior regulatory resolutions, the company added. The disclosure removes some uncertainty related to the probe but the DOJ resolution remains subject to a final agreement and court approval, and Block warned the ultimate terms could result in losses exceeding the amount already accrued.

Source: Reuters

MADRID, Nov 3 : Bayern Munich strengthened their case as Champions League contenders with Tuesday's 2-0 victory at Atletico Madrid, combining defensive discipline with clinical finishing at the stadium that will host the final in June. Facing a determined Diego Simeone side and a partisan crowd, the Bundesliga champions produced a controlled performance despite missing several attacking players and manager Vincent Kompany, who is recovering after collapsing at training. Bayern had drawn 2-2 with Arsenal and 3-3 against Viking in their previous two European matches, leaving victory important to their prospects of finishing in the top eight of the league phase and qualifying directly for the last 16. Last season's semi-finalists Atletico were on a nine-game unbeaten run which included eight wins, but struggled to create clear chances against a compact Bayern defence.

Bayern had conceded at least four goals across the two legs in each of their last four Champions League eliminations, but their defensive cohesion allowed them to control the game until Lennart Karl capitalised on a Robin Le Normand error to open the scoring. "The way we defended together as a group to get the clean sheet, we were really pleased with the whole team performance," Bayern assistant manager Aaron Danks told a press conference. "Tonight was about the collective group, about the spirit of this group, to come together in adversity and get a result in a difficult ground." Harry Kane's pass and the power of Konrad Laimer's finish stood out in Bayern's second goal, but it was their coordinated pressing that forced Atletico into surrendering possession in a dangerous area. Without relying on decisive individual performances or fluid attacking play, Bayern kept the Spanish side at bay with relative ease. Led by Ballon d'Or holder Kane, Bayern possess a squad capable of competing with Europe's leading sides. Paris St Germain's blend of attacking quality and collective discipline has been central to their two Champions League triumphs and Bayern showed at the Metropolitano that they also have the cohesion needed to challenge.

Nov 3 : Meta Platforms said on Tuesday it is raising $15 billion through a five-part US dollar bond offering, as the Facebook parent turns to debt markets to help finance accelerating investments in AI infrastructure. The offering adds to a wave of AI-related fundraising as companies seek capital for data centers, computing capacity and cloud expansion, despite historically relying on strong cash balances to fund growth. It comprises $3.25 billion of notes due in 2031 carrying a 5.85 per cent coupon and another $3.25 billion due in 2033 at 6.25 per cent, according to a regulatory filing. Meta previously tapped debt markets with a $25 billion investment-grade bond sale in April and a $30 billion offering last year, underscoring its growing use of external financing to fund long-term AI investments.

Nov 3 : Canada will not let skaters from Russia or Belarus take part in the world junior ice hockey championships that are due to start next month in the province of Alberta, Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters on Tuesday. Canada, a major international backer of Ukraine in its war with Russia, has already condemned a decision last week by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to allow Russians to compete in International Ice Hockey Federation events. The world junior championships are due to run from late December to early January. "While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he said. "So, if you're asking specifically about the world juniors, the Russians will not be there," he told a televised press conference at the end of a summit in Antigua. Earlier on Tuesday, national ice hockey federations in Norway, Denmark, Sweden and the Czech Republic said they would refuse to play Russia at next year's men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.

MADRID, Nov 3 : Bayern Munich and Paris St Germain underlined their Champions League title credentials with victories over Atletico Madrid and Villarreal respectively on Tuesday, while Manchester United came from two goals down to snatch a dramatic win over AS Roma. Bayern broke down a stubborn Atletico side in Madrid as second-half goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer secured victory, while PSG set a record as the fastest team to score four goals in a Champions League match on their way to a 6-0 victory. At Old Trafford, Matheus Cunha struck twice in quick succession after the break as United overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Roma 3-2, the comeback following protests by home supporters. Barcelona eased to a 3-0 home win over Aston Villa after Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the seventh minute and Raphinha added a second-half double, while Inter Milan were equally convincing, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip.

PSG remain top of the standings with 12 points, followed by a group of six teams on nine points including Barcelona and Villa. Stadiums across Europe fell silent before kickoff in memory of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, who died earlier on Tuesday. At the Metropolitano, Bayern enjoyed the majority of possession but struggled initially to break down a disciplined Atletico side, who finished the first half without a shot on target. That was not a true reflection, however, of the threat the hosts carried on the counter-attack. Bayern's first clear chance did not come until the 22nd minute when Karl shot wide, before an unmarked Harry Kane volleyed off target from close range four minutes later. A series of well-timed defensive interventions prevented Bayern from building momentum, leaving Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak largely untroubled before the break. Karl made the breakthrough after halftime, dispossessing Robin Le Normand inside the Atletico penalty area before finishing neatly. Atletico pushed Bayern back after falling behind but created few clear chances and their determination to play out from defence again proved costly in the 74th minute. Bayern regained possession before Kane's precise pass released Laimer, who produced an equally assured finish to put the result beyond doubt. MANCHESTER UNITED COMEBACK Roma seized control against Manchester United when Matias Soule opened the scoring in the 11th minute, before Donyell Malen doubled their advantage from the penalty spot seven minutes later. The early goals intensified the discontent among the home supporters, who had released hundreds of green and gold balloons as the teams emerged, a reference to United's original colours, before throwing dozens of yellow tennis balls onto the pitch in the first half. United began their fightback in the 58th minute when captain Bruno Fernandes scored a retaken penalty. Cunha then transformed the contest, equalising seven minutes from time before scoring again three minutes later to complete the turnaround and spark jubilant celebrations at Old Trafford. His eventful night ended prematurely, however. Booked for removing his shirt and jumping into the stands after his winner, the Brazilian was sent off for a late challenge in stoppage time, completing a chaotic eight-minute spell. At the Camp Nou, Barcelona's Lamine pounced on a loose Aston Villa pass to open the scoring after seven minutes, although Unai Emery's side created the clearer openings before the break despite pressure from the hosts. Raphinha made the closing stages comfortable for Barcelona with a deflected strike before adding his second from an exquisite Joao Cancelo assist. Inter Milan delivered a clinical away performance to defeat Feyenoord. Yann Bisseck scored early with a long-range curler, before Pio Esposito headed home a second before halftime and Piotr Zielinski sealed the victory. LASK claimed only their second ever Champions League win in a 4-0 triumph over Slovan Bratislava, while hosts Bodo/Glimt drew 0-0 with Lille. Earlier, Aleksey Batrakov scored twice as Galatasaray beat Stuttgart 2-0, while Sporting defeated Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 at Stamford Bridge.

Source: Reuters
